newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.KOREAN WON CLOSES LOWER DESPITE BOK INTERVENTION.
newsitem.headline: S.KOREAN WON CLOSES LOWER DESPITE BOK INTERVENTION.

text.p: The won closed lower against the dollar on Thursday despite the central bank's dollar sales in forward trading due to short-cover dollar buying, dealers said.
The Bank of Korea intervened in the morning, selling dollars in three- and six-month forward trading, they said.
"Some banks were short of dollars despite the central bank's intervention because it was in forward trding," said a domestic bank dealer.
The won closed at 894.80, down from Wednesday's closing of 894.30. It opened at 894.50 and ranged from 894.30 to 895.00.
The market will be closed on Friday on a national holiday.
The won's mid-rate is expected to be pegged at 894.60 on Monday, compared with 894.30 today.
Brokers forecast trading would range from 894.00 to 895.50 early next week.
Dealers said dollars were recently drying up because of rising importer settlements.
